33: Correct: `$user = User::factory()->create(); Event::fake();`
34: 
35: ## Use `recycle()` to Share Relationship Instances Across Factories
36: 
37: Without `recycle()`, nested factories create separate instances of the same conceptual entity.
38: 
39: ```php
40: Ticket::factory()
41:     ->recycle(Airline::factory()->create())
42:     ->create();
43: ```
````

## File: .junie/skills/laravel-best-practices/rules/validation.md
````markdown
 1: # Validation & Forms Best Practices
 2: 
 3: ## Use Form Request Classes
 4: 
 5: Extract validation from controllers into dedicated Form Request classes.
 6: 
 7: Incorrect:
 8: ```php
 9: public function store(Request $request)
10: {
11:     $request->validate([
12:         'title' => 'required|max:255',
13:         'body' => 'required',
14:     ]);
15: }
16: ```
17: 
18: Correct:
19: ```php
20: public function store(StorePostRequest $request)
21: {
22:     Post::create($request->validated());
23: }
24: ```
25: 
26: ## Array vs. String Notation for Rules
27: 
28: Array syntax is more readable and composes cleanly with `Rule::` objects. Prefer it in new code, but check existing Form Requests first and match whatever notation the project already uses.
29: 
30: ```php
31: // Preferred for new code
32: 'email' => ['required', 'email', Rule::unique('users')],
33: 
34: // Follow existing convention if the project uses string notation
35: 'email' => 'required|email|unique:users',
36: ```
37: 
38: ## Always Use `validated()`
39: 
40: Get only validated data. Never use `$request->all()` for mass operations.
41: 
42: Incorrect:
43: ```php
44: Post::create($request->all());
45: ```
46: 
47: Correct:
48: ```php
49: Post::create($request->validated());
50: ```
51: 
52: ## Use `Rule::when()` for Conditional Validation
53: 
54: ```php
55: 'company_name' => [
56:     Rule::when($this->account_type === 'business', ['required', 'string', 'max:255']),
57: ],
58: ```
59: 
60: ## Use the `after()` Method for Custom Validation
61: 
62: Use `after()` instead of `withValidator()` for custom validation logic that depends on multiple fields.
63: 
64: ```php
65: public function after(): array
66: {
67:     return [
68:         function (Validator $validator) {
69:             if ($this->quantity > Product::find($this->product_id)?->stock) {
70:                 $validator->errors()->add('quantity', 'Not enough stock.');
71:             }
72:         },
73:     ];
74: }
75: ```
````

## File: .junie/skills/laravel-best-practices/SKILL.md
````markdown
  1: ---
  2: name: laravel-best-practices
  3: description: "Apply this skill whenever writing, reviewing, or refactoring Laravel PHP code. This includes creating or modifying controllers, models, migrations, form requests, policies, jobs, scheduled commands, service classes, and Eloquent queries. Triggers for N+1 and query performance issues, caching strategies, authorization and security patterns, validation, error handling, queue and job configuration, route definitions, and architectural decisions. Also use for Laravel code reviews and refactoring existing Laravel code to follow best practices. Covers any task involving Laravel backend PHP code patterns."
  4: license: MIT
  5: metadata:
  6:   author: laravel
  7: ---
  8: 
  9: # Laravel Best Practices
 10: 
 11: Best practices for Laravel, prioritized by impact. Each rule teaches what to do and why. For exact API syntax, verify with `search-docs`.
 12: 
 13: ## Consistency First
 14: 
 15: Before applying any rule, check what the application already does. Laravel offers multiple valid approaches — the best choice is the one the codebase already uses, even if another pattern would be theoretically better. Inconsistency is worse than a suboptimal pattern.
 16: 
 17: Check sibling files, related controllers, models, or tests for established patterns. If one exists, follow it — don't introduce a second way. These rules are defaults for when no pattern exists yet, not overrides.
 18: 
 19: ## Quick Reference
 20: 
 21: ### 1. Database Performance → `rules/db-performance.md`
 22: 
 23: - Eager load with `with()` to prevent N+1 queries
 24: - Enable `Model::preventLazyLoading()` in development
 25: - Select only needed columns, avoid `SELECT *`
 26: - `chunk()` / `chunkById()` for large datasets
 27: - Index columns used in `WHERE`, `ORDER BY`, `JOIN`
 28: - `withCount()` instead of loading relations to count
 29: - `cursor()` for memory-efficient read-only iteration
 30: - Never query in Blade templates
 31: 
 32: ### 2. Advanced Query Patterns → `rules/advanced-queries.md`
 33: 
 34: - `addSelect()` subqueries over eager-loading entire has-many for a single value
 35: - Dynamic relationships via subquery FK + `belongsTo`
 36: - Conditional aggregates (`CASE WHEN` in `selectRaw`) over multiple count queries
 37: - `setRelation()` to prevent circular N+1 queries
 38: - `whereIn` + `pluck()` over `whereHas` for better index usage
 39: - Two simple queries can beat one complex query
 40: - Compound indexes matching `orderBy` column order
 41: - Correlated subqueries in `orderBy` for has-many sorting (avoid joins)
 42: 
 43: ### 3. Security → `rules/security.md`
 44: 
 45: - Define `$fillable` or `$guarded` on every model, authorize every action via policies or gates
 46: - No raw SQL with user input — use Eloquent or query builder
 47: - `{{ }}` for output escaping, `@csrf` on all POST/PUT/DELETE forms, `throttle` on auth and API routes
 48: - Validate MIME type, extension, and size for file uploads
 49: - Never commit `.env`, use `config()` for secrets, `encrypted` cast for sensitive DB fields
 50: 
 51: ### 4. Caching → `rules/caching.md`
 52: 
 53: - `Cache::remember()` over manual get/put
 54: - `Cache::flexible()` for stale-while-revalidate on high-traffic data
 55: - `Cache::memo()` to avoid redundant cache hits within a request
 56: - Cache tags to invalidate related groups
 57: - `Cache::add()` for atomic conditional writes
 58: - `once()` to memoize per-request or per-object lifetime
 59: - `Cache::lock()` / `lockForUpdate()` for race conditions
 60: - Failover cache stores in production
 61: 
 62: ### 5. Eloquent Patterns → `rules/eloquent.md`
 63: 
 64: - Correct relationship types with return type hints
 65: - Local scopes for reusable query constraints
 66: - Global scopes sparingly — document their existence
 67: - Attribute casts in the `casts()` method
 68: - Cast date columns, use Carbon instances in templates
 69: - `whereBelongsTo($model)` for cleaner queries
 70: - Never hardcode table names — use `(new Model)->getTable()` or Eloquent queries
 71: 
 72: ### 6. Validation & Forms → `rules/validation.md`
 73: 
 74: - Form Request classes, not inline validation
 75: - Array notation `['required', 'email']` for new code; follow existing convention
 76: - `$request->validated()` only — never `$request->all()`
 77: - `Rule::when()` for conditional validation
 78: - `after()` instead of `withValidator()`
 79: 
 80: ### 7. Configuration → `rules/config.md`
 81: 
 82: - `env()` only inside config files
 83: - `App::environment()` or `app()->isProduction()`
 84: - Config, lang files, and constants over hardcoded text
 85: 
 86: ### 8. Testing Patterns → `rules/testing.md`
 87: 
 88: - `LazilyRefreshDatabase` over `RefreshDatabase` for speed
 89: - `assertModelExists()` over raw `assertDatabaseHas()`
 90: - Factory states and sequences over manual overrides
 91: - Use fakes (`Event::fake()`, `Exceptions::fake()`, etc.) — but always after factory setup, not before
 92: - `recycle()` to share relationship instances across factories
 93: 
 94: ### 9. Queue & Job Patterns → `rules/queue-jobs.md`
 95: 
 96: - `retry_after` must exceed job `timeout`; use exponential backoff `[1, 5, 10]`
 97: - `ShouldBeUnique` to prevent duplicates; `ShouldBeUniqueUntilProcessing` for early lock release
 98: - Always implement `failed()`; with `retryUntil()`, set `$tries = 0`
 99: - `RateLimited` middleware for external API calls; `Bus::batch()` for related jobs
100: - Horizon for complex multi-queue scenarios
101: 
102: ### 10. Routing & Controllers → `rules/routing.md`
103: 
104: - Implicit route model binding
105: - Scoped bindings for nested resources
106: - `Route::resource()` or `apiResource()`
107: - Methods under 10 lines — extract to actions/services
108: - Type-hint Form Requests for auto-validation
109: 
110: ### 11. HTTP Client → `rules/http-client.md`
111: 
112: - Explicit `timeout` and `connectTimeout` on every request
113: - `retry()` with exponential backoff for external APIs
114: - Check response status or use `throw()`
115: - `Http::pool()` for concurrent independent requests
116: - `Http::fake()` and `preventStrayRequests()` in tests
117: 
118: ### 12. Events, Notifications & Mail → `rules/events-notifications.md`, `rules/mail.md`
119: 
120: - Event discovery over manual registration; `event:cache` in production
121: - `ShouldDispatchAfterCommit` / `afterCommit()` inside transactions
122: - Queue notifications and mailables with `ShouldQueue`
123: - On-demand notifications for non-user recipients
124: - `HasLocalePreference` on notifiable models
125: - `assertQueued()` not `assertSent()` for queued mailables
126: - Markdown mailables for transactional emails
127: 
128: ### 13. Error Handling → `rules/error-handling.md`
129: 
130: - `report()`/`render()` on exception classes or in `bootstrap/app.php` — follow existing pattern
131: - `ShouldntReport` for exceptions that should never log
132: - Throttle high-volume exceptions to protect log sinks
133: - `dontReportDuplicates()` for multi-catch scenarios
134: - Force JSON rendering for API routes
135: - Structured context via `context()` on exception classes
136: 
137: ### 14. Task Scheduling → `rules/scheduling.md`
138: 
139: - `withoutOverlapping()` on variable-duration tasks
140: - `onOneServer()` on multi-server deployments
141: - `runInBackground()` for concurrent long tasks
142: - `environments()` to restrict to appropriate environments
143: - `takeUntilTimeout()` for time-bounded processing
144: - Schedule groups for shared configuration
145: 
146: ### 15. Architecture → `rules/architecture.md`
147: 
148: - Single-purpose Action classes; dependency injection over `app()` helper
149: - Prefer official Laravel packages and follow conventions, don't override defaults
150: - Default to `ORDER BY id DESC` or `created_at DESC`; `mb_*` for UTF-8 safety
151: - `defer()` for post-response work; `Context` for request-scoped data; `Concurrency::run()` for parallel execution
152: 
153: ### 16. Migrations → `rules/migrations.md`
154: 
155: - Generate migrations with `php artisan make:migration`
156: - `constrained()` for foreign keys
157: - Never modify migrations that have run in production
158: - Add indexes in the migration, not as an afterthought
159: - Mirror column defaults in model `$attributes`
160: - Reversible `down()` by default; forward-fix migrations for intentionally irreversible changes
161: - One concern per migration — never mix DDL and DML
162: 
163: ### 17. Collections → `rules/collections.md`
164: 
165: - Higher-order messages for simple collection operations
166: - `cursor()` vs. `lazy()` — choose based on relationship needs
167: - `lazyById()` when updating records while iterating
168: - `toQuery()` for bulk operations on collections
169: 
170: ### 18. Blade & Views → `rules/blade-views.md`
171: 
172: - `$attributes->merge()` in component templates
173: - Blade components over `@include`; `@pushOnce` for per-component scripts
174: - View Composers for shared view data
175: - `@aware` for deeply nested component props
176: 
177: ### 19. Conventions & Style → `rules/style.md`
178: 
179: - Follow Laravel naming conventions for all entities
180: - Prefer Laravel helpers (`Str`, `Arr`, `Number`, `Uri`, `Str::of()`, `$request->string()`) over raw PHP functions
181: - No JS/CSS in Blade, no HTML in PHP classes
182: - Code should be readable; comments only for config files
183: 
184: ## How to Apply
185: 
186: Always use a sub-agent to read rule files and explore this skill's content.
187: 
188: 1. Identify the file type and select relevant sections (e.g., migration → §16, controller → §1, §3, §5, §6, §10)
189: 2. Check sibling files for existing patterns — follow those first per Consistency First
190: 3. Verify API syntax with `search-docs` for the installed Laravel version
````

## File: .junie/skills/livewire-development/reference/javascript-hooks.md
````markdown
 1: # Livewire 4 JavaScript Integration
 2: 
 3: ## Interceptor System (v4)
 4: 
 5: ### Intercept Messages
 6: 
 7: ```js
 8: Livewire.interceptMessage(({ component, message, onFinish, onSuccess, onError }) => {
 9:     onFinish(() => { /* After response, before processing */ });
10:     onSuccess(({ payload }) => { /* payload.snapshot, payload.effects */ });
11:     onError(() => { /* Server errors */ });
12: });
13: ```
14: 
15: ### Intercept Requests
16: 
17: ```js
18: Livewire.interceptRequest(({ request, onResponse, onSuccess, onError, onFailure }) => {
19:     onResponse(({ response }) => { /* When received */ });
20:     onSuccess(({ response, responseJson }) => { /* Success */ });
21:     onError(({ response, responseBody, preventDefault }) => { /* 4xx/5xx */ });
22:     onFailure(({ error }) => { /* Network failures */ });
23: });
24: ```
25: 
26: ### Component-Scoped Interceptors
27: 
28: ```blade
29: <script>
30:     this.$intercept('save', ({ component, onSuccess }) => {
31:         onSuccess(() => console.log('Saved!'));
32:     });
33: </script>
34: ```
35: 
36: ## Magic Properties
37: 
38: - `$errors` - Access validation errors from JavaScript
39: - `$intercept` - Component-scoped interceptors
````

## File: .junie/skills/livewire-development/SKILL.md
````markdown
  1: ---
  2: name: livewire-development
  3: description: "Use for any task or question involving Livewire. Activate if user mentions Livewire, wire: directives, or Livewire-specific concepts like wire:model, wire:click, wire:sort, or islands, invoke this skill. Covers building new components, debugging reactivity issues, real-time form validation, drag-and-drop, loading states, migrating from Livewire 3 to 4, converting component formats (SFC/MFC/class-based), and performance optimization. Do not use for non-Livewire reactive UI (React, Vue, Alpine-only, Inertia.js) or standard Laravel forms without Livewire."
  4: license: MIT
  5: metadata:
  6:   author: laravel
  7: ---
  8: 
  9: # Livewire Development
 10: 
 11: ## Documentation
 12: 
 13: Use `search-docs` for detailed Livewire 4 patterns and documentation.
 14: 
 15: ## Basic Usage
 16: 
 17: ### Creating Components
 18: 
 19: ```bash
 20: 
 21: # Single-file component (SFC - default in v4)
 22: 
 23: # Creates: resources/views/components/⚡create-post.blade.php
 24: 
 25: php artisan make:livewire create-post
 26: 
 27: # Page component (SFC - Full Page in v4)
 28: 
 29: # Creates: resources/views/pages/⚡create-post.blade.php
 30: 
 31: php artisan make:livewire pages::create-post
 32: 
 33: # Multi-file component (MFC)
 34: 
 35: # Creates: resources/views/components/⚡create-post/create-post.php
 36: 
 37: #          resources/views/components/⚡create-post/create-post.blade.php
 38: 
 39: php artisan make:livewire create-post --mfc
 40: 
 41: # Class-based component (v3 style)
 42: 
 43: # Creates: app/Livewire/CreatePost.php AND resources/views/livewire/create-post.blade.php
 44: 
 45: php artisan make:livewire create-post --class
 46: 
 47: # With namespace
 48: 
 49: php artisan make:livewire Posts/CreatePost
 50: ```
 51: 
 52: ### Converting Between Formats
 53: 
 54: Use `php artisan livewire:convert create-post` to convert between single-file, multi-file, and class-based formats.
 55: 
 56: ### Choosing a Component Format
 57: 
 58: > **Always follow the project's existing conventions first.** Before creating any component, inspect the project's existing Livewire components to determine the established format (SFC, MFC, or class-based) and directory structure. Check `app/Livewire/`, `resources/views/components/`, and `resources/views/livewire/` for existing components. If the project already uses a consistent format, **use that same format** — even if it differs from the Livewire v4 defaults below. Only fall back to the v4 defaults (SFC in `resources/views/components/`) when no existing convention is established.
 59: 
 60: Also check `config/livewire.php` for `make_command.type`, `make_command.emoji`, `component_locations`, and `component_namespaces` overrides, which change the default format and where files are stored.
 61: 
 62: ### Component Format Reference
 63: 
 64: | Format | Flag | Class Path | View Path |
 65: |--------|------|------------|-----------|
 66: | Single-file (SFC) | default | — | `resources/views/components/⚡create-post.blade.php` (PHP + Blade in one file) |
 67: | Full Page SFC | `pages::name` | — | `resources/views/pages/⚡create-post.blade.php` |
 68: | Multi-file (MFC) | `--mfc` | `resources/views/components/⚡create-post/create-post.php` | `resources/views/components/⚡create-post/create-post.blade.php` |
 69: | Class-based | `--class` | `app/Livewire/CreatePost.php` | `resources/views/livewire/create-post.blade.php` |
 70: | View-based | default (Blade-only) | — | `resources/views/components/⚡create-post.blade.php` (Blade-only with functional state) |
 71: 
 72: > **Important:** The ⚡ prefix shown above is the **default** behavior in Livewire v4 — it is **configurable**. Check `config/livewire.php` for the `make_command.emoji` setting. When `true` (default), always include the ⚡ prefix in filenames you create. When `false`, omit the ⚡ prefix from all paths above.
 73: 
 74: Namespaced components map to subdirectories: `make:livewire Posts/CreatePost` creates `resources/views/components/posts/⚡create-post.blade.php` (single-file by default). Use `make:livewire Posts/CreatePost --mfc` for multi-file output at `resources/views/components/posts/⚡create-post/create-post.php` and `resources/views/components/posts/⚡create-post/create-post.blade.php`.
 75: 
 76: ### Single-File Component Example
 77: 
 78: <!-- Single-File Component Example -->
 79: ```php
 80: <?php
 81: use Livewire\Component;
 82: 
 83: new class extends Component {
 84:     public int $count = 0;
 85: 
 86:     public function increment(): void
 87:     {
 88:         $this->count++;
 89:     }
 90: };
 91: ?>
 92: 
 93: <div>
 94:     <button wire:click="increment">Count: @{{ $count }}</button>
 95: </div>
 96: ```
 97: 
 98: ## Livewire 4 Specifics
 99: 
100: ### Key Changes From Livewire 3
101: 
102: These things changed in Livewire 4, but may not have been updated in this application. Verify this application's setup to ensure you follow existing conventions.
103: 
104: - Use `Route::livewire()` for full-page components (e.g., `Route::livewire('/posts/create', CreatePost::class)`); config keys renamed: `layout` → `component_layout`, `lazy_placeholder` → `component_placeholder`.
105: - `wire:model` now ignores child events by default (use `wire:model.deep` for old behavior); `wire:scroll` renamed to `wire:navigate:scroll`.
106: - Component tags must be properly closed; `wire:transition` now uses View Transitions API (modifiers removed).
107: - JavaScript: `$wire.$js('name', fn)` → `$wire.$js.name = fn`; `commit`/`request` hooks → `interceptMessage()`/`interceptRequest()`.
108: 
109: ### New Features
110: 
111: - Component formats: single-file (SFC), multi-file (MFC), view-based components.
112: - Islands (`@island`) for isolated updates; async actions (`wire:click.async`, `#[Async]`) for parallel execution.
113: - Deferred/bundled loading: `defer`, `lazy.bundle` for optimized component loading.
114: 
115: | Feature | Usage | Purpose |
116: |---------|-------|---------|
117: | Islands | `@island(name: 'stats')` | Isolated update regions |
118: | Async | `wire:click.async` or `#[Async]` | Non-blocking actions |
119: | Deferred | `defer` attribute | Load after page render |
120: | Bundled | `lazy.bundle` | Load multiple together |
121: 
122: ### New Directives
123: 
124: - `wire:sort`, `wire:intersect`, `wire:ref`, `.renderless`, `.preserve-scroll` are available for use.
125: - `data-loading` attribute automatically added to elements triggering network requests.
126: 
127: | Directive | Purpose |
128: |-----------|---------|
129: | `wire:sort` | Drag-and-drop sorting |
130: | `wire:intersect` | Viewport intersection detection |
131: | `wire:ref` | Element references for JS |
132: | `.renderless` | Component without rendering |
133: | `.preserve-scroll` | Preserve scroll position |
134: 
135: ## Best Practices
136: 
137: - Always use `wire:key` in loops
138: - Use `wire:loading` for loading states
139: - Use `wire:model.live` for instant updates (default is debounced)
140: - Validate and authorize in actions (treat like HTTP requests)
141: 
142: ## Configuration
143: 
144: - `smart_wire_keys` defaults to `true`; new configs: `component_locations`, `component_namespaces`, `make_command`, `csp_safe`.
145: 
146: ## Alpine & JavaScript
147: 
148: - `wire:transition` uses browser View Transitions API; `$errors` and `$intercept` magic properties available.
149: - Non-blocking `wire:poll` and parallel `wire:model.live` updates improve performance.
150: 
151: For interceptors and hooks, see [reference/javascript-hooks.md](reference/javascript-hooks.md).
152: 
153: ## Testing
154: 
155: <!-- Testing Example -->
156: ```php
157: Livewire::test(Counter::class)
158:     ->assertSet('count', 0)
159:     ->call('increment')
160:     ->assertSet('count', 1);
161: ```
162: 
163: ## Verification
164: 
165: 1. Browser console: Check for JS errors
166: 2. Network tab: Verify Livewire requests return 200
167: 3. Ensure `wire:key` on all `@foreach` loops
168: 
169: ## Common Pitfalls
170: 
171: - Missing `wire:key` in loops → unexpected re-rendering
172: - Expecting `wire:model` real-time → use `wire:model.live`
173: - Unclosed component tags → syntax errors in v4
174: - Using deprecated config keys or JS hooks
175: - Including Alpine.js separately (already bundled in Livewire 4)
````

## File: .junie/skills/tailwindcss-development/SKILL.md
````markdown
  1: ---
  2: name: tailwindcss-development
  3: description: "Always invoke when the user's message includes 'tailwind' in any form. Also invoke for: building responsive grid layouts (multi-column card grids, product grids), flex/grid page structures (dashboards with sidebars, fixed topbars, mobile-toggle navs), styling UI components (cards, tables, navbars, pricing sections, forms, inputs, badges), adding dark mode variants, fixing spacing or typography, and Tailwind v3/v4 work. The core use case: writing or fixing Tailwind utility classes in HTML templates (Blade, JSX, Vue). Skip for backend PHP logic, database queries, API routes, JavaScript with no HTML/CSS component, CSS file audits, build tool configuration, and vanilla CSS."
  4: license: MIT
  5: metadata:
  6:   author: laravel
  7: ---
  8: 
  9: # Tailwind CSS Development
 10: 
 11: ## Documentation
 12: 
 13: Use `search-docs` for detailed Tailwind CSS v4 patterns and documentation.
 14: 
 15: ## Basic Usage
 16: 
 17: - Use Tailwind CSS classes to style HTML. Check and follow existing Tailwind conventions in the project before introducing new patterns.
 18: - Offer to extract repeated patterns into components that match the project's conventions (e.g., Blade, JSX, Vue).
 19: - Consider class placement, order, priority, and defaults. Remove redundant classes, add classes to parent or child elements carefully to reduce repetition, and group elements logically.
 20: 
 21: ## Tailwind CSS v4 Specifics
 22: 
 23: - Always use Tailwind CSS v4 and avoid deprecated utilities.
 24: - `corePlugins` is not supported in Tailwind v4.
 25: 
 26: ### CSS-First Configuration
 27: 
 28: In Tailwind v4, configuration is CSS-first using the `@theme` directive — no separate `tailwind.config.js` file is needed:
 29: 
 30: <!-- CSS-First Config -->
 31: ```css
 32: @theme {
 33:   --color-brand: oklch(0.72 0.11 178);
 34: }
 35: ```
 36: 
 37: ### Import Syntax
 38: 
 39: In Tailwind v4, import Tailwind with a regular CSS `@import` statement instead of the `@tailwind` directives used in v3:
 40: 
 41: <!-- v4 Import Syntax -->
 42: ```diff
 43: - @tailwind base;
 44: - @tailwind components;
 45: - @tailwind utilities;
 46: + @import "tailwindcss";
 47: ```
 48: 
 49: ### Replaced Utilities
 50: 
 51: Tailwind v4 removed deprecated utilities. Use the replacements shown below. Opacity values remain numeric.
 52: 
 53: | Deprecated | Replacement |
 54: |------------|-------------|
 55: | bg-opacity-* | bg-black/* |
 56: | text-opacity-* | text-black/* |
 57: | border-opacity-* | border-black/* |
 58: | divide-opacity-* | divide-black/* |
 59: | ring-opacity-* | ring-black/* |
 60: | placeholder-opacity-* | placeholder-black/* |
 61: | flex-shrink-* | shrink-* |
 62: | flex-grow-* | grow-* |
 63: | overflow-ellipsis | text-ellipsis |
 64: | decoration-slice | box-decoration-slice |
 65: | decoration-clone | box-decoration-clone |
 66: 
 67: ## Spacing
 68: 
 69: Use `gap` utilities instead of margins for spacing between siblings:
 70: 
 71: <!-- Gap Utilities -->
 72: ```html
 73: <div class="flex gap-8">
 74:     <div>Item 1</div>
 75:     <div>Item 2</div>
 76: </div>
 77: ```
 78: 
 79: ## Dark Mode
 80: 
 81: If existing pages and components support dark mode, new pages and components must support it the same way, typically using the `dark:` variant:
 82: 
 83: <!-- Dark Mode -->
 84: ```html
 85: <div class="bg-white dark:bg-gray-900 text-gray-900 dark:text-white">
 86:     Content adapts to color scheme
 87: </div>
 88: ```
 89: 
 90: ## Common Patterns
 91: 
 92: ### Flexbox Layout
 93: 
 94: <!-- Flexbox Layout -->
 95: ```html
 96: <div class="flex items-center justify-between gap-4">
 97:     <div>Left content</div>
 98:     <div>Right content</div>
 99: </div>
100: ```
101: 
102: ### Grid Layout
103: 
104: <!-- Grid Layout -->
105: ```html
106: <div class="grid grid-cols-1 md:grid-cols-2 lg:grid-cols-3 gap-6">
107:     <div>Card 1</div>
108:     <div>Card 2</div>
109:     <div>Card 3</div>
110: </div>
111: ```
112: 
113: ## Common Pitfalls
114: 
115: - Using deprecated v3 utilities (bg-opacity-*, flex-shrink-*, etc.)
116: - Using `@tailwind` directives instead of `@import "tailwindcss"`
117: - Trying to use `tailwind.config.js` instead of CSS `@theme` directive
118: - Using margins for spacing between siblings instead of gap utilities
119: - Forgetting to add dark mode variants when the project uses dark mode
````

## File: app/Models/AppointmentReminderPreference.php
````php
  1: <?php
  2: 
  3: namespace App\Models;
  4: 
  5: use Illuminate\Database\Eloquent\Model;
  6: use Illuminate\Support\Collection;
  7: 
  8: use function collect;
  9: 
 10: class AppointmentReminderPreference extends Model
 11: {
 12:     public const CHANNEL_WHATSAPP = 'whatsapp';
 13: 
 14:     public const CHANNEL_EMAIL = 'email';
 15: 
 16:     protected $fillable = [
 17:         'channel',
 18:         'lead_days',
 19:         'enabled',
 20:     ];
 21: 
 22:     protected function casts(): array
 23:     {
 24:         return [
 25:             'enabled' => 'boolean',
 26:             'lead_days' => 'integer',
 27:         ];
 28:     }
 29: 
 30:     /**
 31:      * @return array<int, string>
 32:      */
 33:     public static function leadDayOptions(): array
 34:     {
 35:         return [
 36:             1 => '1 día antes',
 37:             2 => '2 días antes',
 38:             3 => '3 días antes',
 39:             7 => '1 semana antes',
 40:         ];
 41:     }
 42: 
 43:     /**
 44:      * @return list<string>
 45:      */
 46:     public static function channels(): array
 47:     {
 48:         return [
 49:             self::CHANNEL_WHATSAPP,
 50:             self::CHANNEL_EMAIL,
 51:         ];
 52:     }
 53: 
 54:     /**
 55:      * @return list<int>
 56:      */
 57:     public static function enabledLeadDaysFor(string $channel): array
 58:     {
 59:         $preferences = static::query()
 60:             ->where('channel', $channel)
 61:             ->orderBy('lead_days')
 62:             ->get();
 63: 
 64:         if ($preferences->isEmpty()) {
 65:             return static::defaultLeadDaysFor($channel);
 66:         }
 67: 
 68:         return static::selectedLeadDays($preferences);
 69:     }
 70: 
 71:     /**
 72:      * @return array<string, list<int>>
 73:      */
 74:     public static function selections(): array
 75:     {
 76:         $preferences = static::query()
 77:             ->whereIn('channel', static::channels())
 78:             ->get()
 79:             ->groupBy('channel');
 80: 
 81:         return collect(static::channels())
 82:             ->mapWithKeys(fn (string $channel): array => [
 83:                 $channel => $preferences->has($channel)
 84:                     ? static::selectedLeadDays($preferences->get($channel, collect()))
 85:                     : static::defaultLeadDaysFor($channel),
 86:             ])
 87:             ->all();
 88:     }
 89: 
 90:     /**
 91:      * @param  array<string, list<int>>  $selections
 92:      */
 93:     public static function saveSelections(array $selections): void
 94:     {
 95:         foreach (static::channels() as $channel) {
 96:             $selectedLeadDays = collect($selections[$channel] ?? [])
 97:                 ->map(fn ($leadDays) => (int) $leadDays)
 98:                 ->intersect(array_keys(static::leadDayOptions()))
 99:                 ->values();
100: 
101:             foreach (array_keys(static::leadDayOptions()) as $leadDays) {
102:                 static::query()->updateOrCreate(
103:                     [
104:                         'channel' => $channel,
105:                         'lead_days' => $leadDays,
106:                     ],
107:                     [
108:                         'enabled' => $selectedLeadDays->contains($leadDays),
109:                     ],
110:                 );
111:             }
112:         }
113:     }
114: 
115:     /**
116:      * @param  Collection<int, self>  $preferences
117:      * @return list<int>
118:      */
119:     private static function selectedLeadDays(Collection $preferences): array
120:     {
121:         return $preferences
122:             ->where('enabled', true)
123:             ->pluck('lead_days')
124:             ->map(fn ($leadDays) => (int) $leadDays)
125:             ->sort()
126:             ->values()
127:             ->all();
128:     }
129: 
130:     /**
131:      * @return list<int>
132:      */
133:     private static function defaultLeadDaysFor(string $channel): array
134:     {
135:         return $channel === self::CHANNEL_WHATSAPP ? [1] : [];
136:     }
137: }
````

40: 
41:   {{ $slot }}
42: </button>

## File: .agents/skills/laravel-blade-components-and-layouts/SKILL.md
````markdown
 1: ---
 2: name: laravel:blade-components-and-layouts
 3: description: Compose UIs with Blade components, slots, and layouts; keep templates pure and testable
 4: ---
 5: 
 6: # Blade Components and Layouts
 7: 
 8: Encapsulate markup and behavior with components; prefer slots over includes.
 9: 
10: ## Commands
11: 
12: ```
13: sail artisan make:component Alert              # or: php artisan make:component Alert
14: 
15: // Use component
16: <x-alert type="warning" :message="$msg" class="mb-4" />
17: 
18: // Layouts + stacks
19: @extends('layouts.app')
20: @push('scripts')
21:     <script>/* page script */</script>
22: @endpush
23: ```
24: 
25: ## Patterns
26: 
27: - Keep components dumb: pass data in, emit markup out
28: - Use `merge()` to honor passed classes/attributes in components
29: - Prefer named slots for readability
30: - Extract small, reusable atoms rather than giant organisms
31: - Laravel 13+: use the `@fonts` directive (with the Vite font plugin) in layout `<head>` to emit preload links and `@font-face` rules automatically; `@fonts(["sans", "mono"])` for a subset
````

  1: # Plan: Critical Security & Reliability Fixes
  2: 
  3: ## Overview
  4: Fix 3 critical issues: hardcoded admin, missing authorization, synchronous WhatsApp sends. Issue #4 (webhook CSRF) is already handled in `bootstrap/app.php:20-22`.
  5: 
  6: ---
  7: 
  8: ## Issue 1: Admin Hardcoded to User ID 1
  9: 
 10: **Problem**: `EnsureUserIsAdmin.php:15` checks `(int) $user->id === 1`. If user 1 is deleted, no admin can exist.

## File: .mimocode/plans/1783256367389-lucky-lagoon.md
````markdown
 1: # Plan: Vincular respuestas de Twilio al mensaje original via ParentMessageSid
 2: 
 3: ## Problema
 4: 
 5: Cuando un cliente responde a un WhatsApp enviado, el webhook de Twilio incluye un campo `ParentMessageSid` con el SID del mensaje original. Actualmente la app ignora ese campo y busca la respuesta por telefono + mensaje enviado mas reciente sin respuesta (`TwilioWhatsAppStatusController:77-82`). Esto es fragil: si un cliente tiene varios mensajes enviados, puede vincularse al equivocado.
 6: 
 7: ## Solucion
 8: 
 9: Usar `ParentMessageSid` del webhook para encontrar el mensaje original exacto via `provider_message_id`. Si el campo no esta presente (respuesta libre, no boton), mantener el fallback actual.
10: 
11: ## Archivos a modificar
12: 
13: ### 1. `app/Http/Controllers/Webhooks/TwilioWhatsAppStatusController.php`
14: 
15: En `processInboundMessage()`:
16: 
17: - Extraer `ParentMessageSid` del payload (Twilio lo envia cuando la respuesta viene de un boton de plantilla)
18: - Primero buscar el mensaje original por `provider_message_id = ParentMessageSid`
19: - Si se encuentra, usar ese mensaje directamente
20: - Si no, usar el fallback actual (telefono + mas reciente sin respuesta)
21: - Guardar `ParentMessageSid` y `ConversationSid` en `provider_payload.inbound` para trazabilidad
22: - Actualizar el log para incluir el SID del mensaje padre vinculado
23: 
24: ```php
25: // Nuevo orden de busqueda:
26: // 1. Por ParentMessageSid (match exacto)
27: $parentSid = trim((string) data_get($payload, 'ParentMessageSid', ''));
28: $message = null;
29: if ($parentSid !== '') {
30:     $message = WhatsAppMessage::query()
31:         ->where('provider_message_id', $parentSid)
32:         ->whereNull('respuesta')
33:         ->where('status', WhatsAppMessage::STATUS_SENT)
34:         ->first();
35: }
36: // 2. Fallback: telefono + mas reciente sin respuesta
37: if (! $message) {
38:     $message = WhatsAppMessage::query()
39:         ->where('telefono', $phone)
40:         ->whereNull('respuesta')
41:         ->where('status', WhatsAppMessage::STATUS_SENT)
42:         ->latest('sent_at')
43:         ->first();
44: }
45: ```
46: 
47: En el array `provider_payload.inbound`, agregar:
48: - `'parent_message_sid'` — SID del mensaje padre (Twilio)
49: - `'conversation_sid'` — SID de la conversacion (Twilio)
50: 
51: En el log, agregar `parent_message_sid` y `conversation_sid` para facilitar la trazabilidad.
52: 
53: ### 2. Tests: `tests/Feature/TwilioWhatsAppStatusWebhookTest.php`
54: 
55: Agregar tests que verifiquen:
56: - Respuesta con `ParentMessageSid` se vincula al mensaje correcto aunque existan otros mensajes enviados al mismo telefono
57: - Respuesta sin `ParentMessageSid` sigue usando el fallback (telefono + mas reciente)
58: - El `provider_payload.inbound` contiene los campos `parent_message_sid` y `conversation_sid`
59: 
60: ### 3. `app/Services/WhatsApp/WhatsAppResponseHandler.php`
61: 
62: Sin cambios. Recibe el `WhatsAppMessage` ya vinculado.
63: 
64: ### 4. `app/Models/WhatsAppMessage.php`
65: 
66: Sin cambios. Los campos ya existen en el esquema.
67: 
68: ## No se necesitan migraciones
69: 
70: Los campos `parent_message_sid` y `conversation_sid` se guardan dentro del JSON `provider_payload` que ya existe.
71: 
72: ## Verificacion
73: 
74: ```bash
75: # Formatear
76: vendor/bin/pint --dirty --format agent
77: 
78: # Tests
79: php artisan test --compact tests/Feature/TwilioWhatsAppStatusWebhookTest.php
80: php artisan test --compact --filter=TwilioWhatsAppStatus
81: ```
````

## File: .mimocode/plans/1783282400248-quiet-planet.md
````markdown
 1: # Fix: WhatsApp button responses not registered on production server
 2: 
 3: ## Root Cause
 4: 
 5: The Twilio WhatsApp **sandbox** uses the Conversations API and has its own inbound webhook URL, separate from the Messaging Service webhook. This sandbox webhook is likely still pointing to the local ngrok URL (`https://chery-precranial-extemporarily.ngrok-free.dev/...`). When a client clicks "Confirmar" or "Reprogramar", Twilio sends the inbound message to the sandbox's own webhook URL — NOT to the Messaging Service URL that is correctly configured at `https://juanjota.eu/webhooks/twilio/whatsapp-status`.
 6: 
 7: This explains why:
 8: - Messages are **sent** successfully (outbound uses the API payload, which has the correct StatusCallback)
 9: - Delivery status updates may work (StatusCallback in API payload)
10: - But **inbound responses** never reach the server (sandbox webhook points to ngrok)
11: 
12: ## Solution Options
13: 
14: ### Option A: Update sandbox webhook URL in Twilio Console (no code change)
15: 
16: The sandbox webhook configuration is in a specific location in Twilio Console:
17: 
18: 1. Go to **console.twilio.com**
19: 2. Navigate to **Messaging → Try it out → Send a WhatsApp message**
20: 3. On the **"Send & receive"** tab (not the "Logs" tab the user was viewing)
21: 4. Scroll down to **"Sandbox Configuration"** section
22: 5. Set **"When a message comes in"** to `https://juanjota.eu/webhooks/twilio/whatsapp-status`
23: 6. Set method to **HTTP POST**
24: 7. Click **Save**
25: 
26: This is the simplest fix — no code changes needed.
27: 
28: ### Option B: Add a Twilio API call to configure sandbox webhook (code change)
29: 
30: If the user can't find or edit the sandbox configuration in the Console UI, add a command/helper that uses the Twilio Conversations API to update the sandbox webhook URL programmatically.
31: 
32: **File to modify:** `app/Services/WhatsApp/WhatsAppSender.php` or a new artisan command
33: 
34: The Twilio API endpoint to update sandbox configuration:
35: ```
36: PUT https://conversations.twilio.com/v1/Conversations/{ConversationSid}
37: ```
38: 
39: Or update the default conversation role webhook:
40: ```
41: POST https://conversations.twilio.com/v1/Services/{ServiceSid}/Configuration
42: ```
43: 
44: ### Option C: Switch server to sender mode (recommended for production)
45: 
46: Change `TWILIO_WHATSAPP_MODE=sender` on the server and configure `TWILIO_WHATSAPP_FROM` with the real sender number. Sender mode uses the Messaging Service webhook (already correctly configured), bypassing the sandbox entirely.
47: 
48: **.env change on server:**
49: ```

## File: .mimocode/plans/1783290993228-swift-falcon.md
````markdown
  1: # Plan: Diagnosticar y reparar envío de WhatsApp en producción
  2: 
  3: ## Contexto
  4: 
  5: La sesión anterior identificó que los botones de WhatsApp (Confirmar/Reprogramar) no funcionan en producción porque el sender pertenece a "Default Messaging Service for Conversations" de Twilio, y la Conversations API ignora la configuración de webhook del sender. Ahora el usuario reporta un problema **nuevo**: los mensajes ni siquiera se envían (no llegan al teléfono), sin error visible.
  6: 
  7: ## Hipótesis
  8: 
  9: Posibles causas de que no envíe WhatsApp sin error:
 10: 
 11: 1. **`WHATSAPP_DRIVER=log` en el servidor** — El job ejecuta pero solo loguea, no envía a Twilio
 12: 2. **`WHATSAPP_MESSAGE_MODE=template` sin Content SID válido** — Twilio rechaza porque la plantilla no existe o no está aprobada
 13: 3. **`TWILIO_WHATSAPP_FROM` incorrecto** — El número from no coincide con el sender registrado en Twilio
 14: 4. **Credenciales de Twilio inválidas** — Account SID o Auth Token cambiados/revocados
 15: 5. **Twilio bloqueó el sender** — Por uso inapropiado o restricciones de sandbox
 16: 
 17: ## Pasos de diagnóstico (en el servidor de producción)
 18: 
 19: ### Paso 1: Verificar configuración del .env en el servidor
 20: 
 21: ```bash
 22: ssh juanjota@pserver2
 23: cd /home/juanjota/public_html_backup
 24: grep -E "(WHATSAPP_DRIVER|TWILIO_WHATSAPP_MODE|TWILIO_WHATSAPP_FROM|WHATSAPP_MESSAGE_MODE|TWILIO_CONTENT_SID|TWILIO_ACCOUNT_SID|TWILIO_AUTH_TOKEN)" .env
 25: ```
 26: 
 27: **Esperado para envío funcional:**
 28: - `WHATSAPP_DRIVER=twilio`
 29: - `TWILIO_WHATSAPP_MODE=sender` (o `sandbox`)
 30: - `TWILIO_WHATSAPP_FROM=whatsapp:+XXXXXXXXX` (número real registrado)
 31: - `TWILIO_ACCOUNT_SID` y `TWILIO_AUTH_TOKEN` presentes y correctos
 32: 
 33: ### Paso 2: Verificar logs de errores de WhatsApp
 34: 
 35: ```bash
 36: cat storage/logs/laravel.log | grep -i "whatsapp\|twilio" | tail -20
 37: ```
 38: 
 39: Si hay errores de Twilio (credenciales inválidas, plantilla no encontrada, sender bloqueado), aparecerán aquí.
 40: 
 41: ### Paso 3: Probar envío directo vía curl desde el servidor
 42: 
 43: ```bash
 44: # Reemplazar con las credenciales reales del .env
 45: curl -s -u "ACCOUNT_SID:AUTH_TOKEN" \
 46:   -X POST "https://api.twilio.com/2010-04-01/Accounts/ACCOUNT_SID/Messages.json" \
 47:   -d "From=whatsapp:+15559355880" \
 48:   -d "To=whatsapp:+34XXXXXXXXX" \
 49:   -d "Body=Prueba de envío directo" \
 50:   -d "StatusCallback=https://juanjota.eu/webhooks/twilio/whatsapp-status"
 51: ```
 52: 
 53: Si esto funciona → el problema está en la configuración de Laravel (driver, message_mode, etc.)
 54: Si esto falla → el problema está en Twilio (credenciales, sender, restricciones)
 55: 
 56: ### Paso 4: Verificar si el sender +15559355880 sigue activo
 57: 
 58: En Twilio Console → **Messaging → Senders → WhatsApp senders** → verificar que el sender esté "Online" y no tenga restricciones.
 59: 
 60: ## Solución según diagnóstico
 61: 
 62: ### Si `WHATSAPP_DRIVER=log` en producción:
 63: Cambiar a `WHATSAPP_DRIVER=twilio` en el `.env` del servidor y ejecutar:
 64: ```bash
 65: php artisan config:cache
 66: ```
 67: 
 68: ### Si `WHATSAPP_MESSAGE_MODE=template` pero el Content SID no es válido:
 69: - **Opción A**: Cambiar a `WHATSAPP_MESSAGE_MODE=text` para enviar mensajes de texto plano
 70: - **Opción B**: Verificar/corregir el Content SID en Twilio Console → **Content API → Content Templates**
 71: 
 72: ### Si el sender +15559355880 no está activo o tiene restricciones:
 73: - Verificar en Twilio Console que el sender esté "Online"
 74: - Si fue desactivado, reactivarlo o usar otro sender
 75: 
 76: ### Si credenciales inválidas:
 77: Actualizar `TWILIO_ACCOUNT_SID` y `TWILIO_AUTH_TOKEN` en el `.env` del servidor
 78: 
 79: ## Archivos relevantes
 80: 
 81: - `app/Services/WhatsApp/WhatsAppSender.php` — Lógica de envío, resolución de modo
 82: - `app/Jobs/SendWhatsAppMessage.php` — Job que ejecuta el envío
 83: - `config/whatsapp.php` — Configuración del driver y Twilio
 84: - `.env` en el servidor — Variables de entorno (solo en producción)
 85: 
 86: ## Verificación
 87: 
 88: 1. Después de corregir la configuración, ejecutar `php artisan config:cache` en el servidor
 89: 2. Enviar un WhatsApp de prueba desde la interfaz de la app
 90: 3. Verificar que el mensaje llegue al teléfono
 91: 4. Verificar en la base de datos que `whatsapp_messages.status = 'sent'`
 92: 5. Verificar en Twilio Console → **Monitor → Logs** que el mensaje aparezca como "Sent"
 93: 
 94: ## Paso 5 (post-fix): Resolver el problema de webhooks inbound
 95: 
 96: Una vez que el envío funcione, volver al problema original: los botones Confirmar/Reprogramar no se registran en producción. La solución es configurar el webhook de la Conversations API:
 97: 
 98: **Opción A (recomendada)**: Configurar webhook vía API de Twilio:
 99: ```bash
100: # 1. Obtener el Service SID de Conversations
101: curl -s -u "ACCOUNT_SID:AUTH_TOKEN" \
102:   "https://api.twilio.com/2010-04-01/Accounts/ACCOUNT_SID/Conversations/Services.json"
103: 
104: # 2. Actualizar el webhook del servicio
105: curl -s -u "ACCOUNT_SID:AUTH_TOKEN" \
106:   -X POST "https://api.twilio.com/2010-04-01/Accounts/ACCOUNT_SID/Conversations/Services/SERVICE_SID" \
107:   -d "MessagingService.OnMessageAddedUrl=https://juanjota.eu/webhooks/twilio/whatsapp-status" \
108:   -d "MessagingService.OnMessageAddedMethod=POST"
109: ```
110: 
111: **Opción B**: Quitar el sender del servicio de Conversations para usar Programmable Messaging estándar.
````

## File: .mimocode/plans/1783456328338-eager-rocket.md
````markdown
  1: # Plan: Mover credenciales Twilio de .env a Base de Datos
  2: 
  3: ## Contexto
  4: 
  5: Actualmente todas las credenciales Twilio viven en `.env` → `config/whatsapp.php`. Para cambiarlas hay que SSHear al servidor, editar `.env`, limpiar cache y reiniciar. Con la DB se pueden editar desde Ajustes sin tocar el servidor.
  6: 
  7: ## Análisis de riesgo
  8: 
  9: | Aspecto | .env (actual) | BD (propuesto) |
 10: |---------|---------------|----------------|
 11: | Seguridad | Archivo en disco, solo accesible por SSH | Cifrado con Laravel `encrypted` cast, expuesto a SQL injection |
 12: | Edición | Requiere SSH + config:clear | desde UI en `/admin/settings` |
 13: | Multi-tenant | No aplica | No necesario (single-clinic) |
 14: | Fallback | N/A | Si DB vacía → usar .env |
 15: 
 16: **Decisión**: Proceder con cifrado `encrypted` cast. La app es single-tenant y el beneficio de editar desde UI supera el riesgo marginal (el admin ya tiene acceso a la BD).
 17: 
 18: ## Tabla: `whatsapp_credentials`
 19: 
 20: Migración `2026_07_08_000000_create_whatsapp_credentials_table.php`:
 21: 
 22: ```sql
 23: whatsapp_credentials:
 24:   id (bigint, PK)
 25:   account_sid (string, nullable, encrypted)
 26:   auth_token (string, nullable, encrypted)
 27:   api_key_sid (string, nullable, encrypted)
 28:   api_key_secret (string, nullable, encrypted)
 29:   messaging_service_sid (string, nullable, encrypted)
 30:   from_number (string, nullable)
 31:   test_recipient (string, nullable)
 32:   timestamps
 33: ```
 34: 
 35: Singleton pattern (un solo registro). Los campos sensibles usan `Encrypted` cast de Laravel.
 36: 
 37: ## Modelo: `App\Models\WhatsAppCredential`
 38: 
 39: ```php
 40: protected $table = 'whatsapp_credentials';
 41: 
 42: protected function casts(): array {
 43:     return [
 44:         'account_sid' => 'encrypted',
 45:         'auth_token' => 'encrypted',
 46:         'api_key_sid' => 'encrypted',
 47:         'api_key_secret' => 'encrypted',
 48:         'messaging_service_sid' => 'encrypted',
 49:     ];
 50: }
 51: 
 52: public static function get(): static { ... }
 53: public function toConfigArray(): array { ... }
 54: ```
 55: 
 56: ## Resolución de config: DB → .env fallback
 57: 
 58: Crear `App\Support\TwilioConfig`:
 59: 
 60: ```php
 61: public static function resolve(string $key): mixed
 62: {
 63:     $dbValue = WhatsAppCredential::get()->{$key} ?? null;
 64:     return $dbValue ?: config("whatsapp.twilio.{$key}");
 65: }
 66: ```
 67: 
 68: Modificar `WhatsAppSender`, `AppointmentDeliveryStatusSyncer`, `TwilioWhatsAppStatusController` para que usen `TwilioConfig::resolve()` en lugar de `config('whatsapp.twilio.X')`.
 69: 
 70: ## Archivos a modificar
 71: 
 72: | Archivo | Cambio |
 73: |---------|--------|
 74: | `config/whatsapp.php` | Sin cambios (mantiene .env como fallback) |
 75: | `app/Models/WhatsAppCredential.php` | **Nuevo** — modelo singleton con `encrypted` casts |
 76: | `app/Support/TwilioConfig.php` | **Nuevo** — resolvedor DB → env |
 77: | `app/Services/WhatsApp/WhatsAppSender.php` | Usar `TwilioConfig::resolve()` en `sendTwilioRequest()`, `buildTwilioPayload()`, `resolveTwilioMode()` |
 78: | `app/Services/WhatsApp/AppointmentDeliveryStatusSyncer.php` | Usar `TwilioConfig::resolve()` en `refreshMessageFromTwilio()` |
 79: | `app/Http/Controllers/Webhooks/TwilioWhatsAppStatusController.php` | Usar `TwilioConfig::resolve()` para `auth_token` en `isValidTwilioRequest()` |
 80: | `resources/views/settings/index.blade.php` | Agregar sección editable para credenciales (inputs para SID, token, from, etc.) |
 81: | `app/Livewire/TwilioCredentialSettings.php` | **Nuevo** — componente Livewire para gestionar credenciales |
 82: 
 83: ## UI en Ajustes
 84: 
 85: Nueva sección "Credenciales Twilio" con:
 86: - Input Account SID (máscara al guardar, mostrar parcial)
 87: - Input Auth Token (password field, solo "Configurado/No configurado" al mostrar)
 88: - Input API Key SID (opcional)
 89: - Input API Key Secret (opcional, password)
 90: - Input Messaging Service SID (opcional)
 91: - Input From Number
 92: - Input Test Recipient
 93: - Botón Guardar
 94: 
 95: ## Verificación
 96: 1. `php artisan migrate` — crear tabla
 97: 2. Guardar credenciales desde Ajustes → se cifran en BD
 98: 3. Enviar WhatsApp de prueba → funciona con credenciales de BD
 99: 4. Borrar credenciales de BD → fallback a .env
100: 5. `vendor/bin/pint --dirty --format agent`
101: 6. Tests existentes pasan (usan config mock, no .env real)
````

 1: # Plan: Settings Backup/Restore
 2: 
 3: ## Goal
 4: Create a seeder with defaults + JSON export/import for all 6 settings tables.
 5: 
 6: ## Files to create
 7: 
 8: ### 1. `database/seeders/SettingsSeeder.php`
 9: Seeds all 6 tables with factory defaults. Uses `updateOrCreate` to be idempotent.
10: 
11: **Defaults per table:**
12: 
13: | Table | Defaults |
14: |---|---|
15: | `sistema_opciones` | `retention_period: 'disabled'` |
16: | `whatsapp_dispatch_settings` | `enabled: true`, `hours: ['09:00','12:00','15:00']` |
17: | `appointment_reminder_preferences` | whatsapp: [1,2,3,7] enabled; email: [] all disabled |
18: | `whatsapp_credentials` | `mode: 'sandbox'`, `selected: true` |
19: | `whatsapp_sender_numbers` | empty (depends on user's actual numbers) |
20: | `twilio_content_templates` | delegates to existing `TwilioContentTemplateSeeder` |
21: 
22: ### 2. `app/Console/Commands/SettingsExport.php`
23: Artisan command: `settings:export {path?}`
24: 
25: - Defaults to `storage/app/settings-backup.json`
26: - Exports all 6 tables as JSON with version + timestamp metadata
27: - Decrypts encrypted fields (account_sid, auth_token, api_key_sid, api_key_secret, cloud_api_access_token) before writing so the backup is portable across environments
28: - Output: JSON file with structure:
29:   ```json
30:   {
31:     "version": 1,
32:     "exported_at": "ISO8601",
33:     "settings": {
34:       "sistema_opciones": { ... },
35:       "whatsapp_dispatch_settings": { ... },
36:       "appointment_reminder_preferences": [ ... ],
37:       "whatsapp_credentials": { ... },
38:       "whatsapp_sender_numbers": [ ... ],
39:       "twilio_content_templates": [ ... ]
40:     }
41:   }
42:   ```
43: 
44: ### 3. `app/Console/Commands/SettingsImport.php`
45: Artisan command: `settings:import {path?} {--force}`
46: 
47: - Reads JSON file (same structure as export)
48: - Validates version field
49: - Without `--force`: shows diff of what will change, asks for confirmation
50: - With `--force`: applies changes directly
51: - Re-encrypts the 5 encrypted credential fields on import
52: - Uses `DB::transaction` for atomicity
53: - Preserves IDs when present in JSON (upsert behavior)
54: 
55: ## Files to modify
56: 
57: ### 4. `database/seeders/DatabaseSeeder.php`
58: Add `$this->call(SettingsSeeder::class);` — but AFTER TwilioContentTemplateSeeder since SettingsSeeder will skip templates (already seeded).
59: 
60: ## Verification
61: 
62: 1. `php artisan settings:export` → check JSON file created
63: 2. Modify a setting via UI, re-export, verify change appears
64: 3. `php artisan settings:import storage/app/settings-backup.json --force` → verify all settings restored
65: 4. `php artisan db:seed --class=SettingsSeeder` → verify idempotent (run twice, same result)
66: 5. `php artisan test --compact` → all tests pass
````

 4:

Esto significa que un export→import completo pierde datos de configuración.

 1: # Plan: Webhook toggle + poll interval configurable
 2: 
 3: ## Objetivo
 4: Cuando el webhook está configurado → llegan datos vía webhook (instantáneo).
 5: Cuando NO hay webhook → poll a la API de Twilio cada X segundos (configurable).
 6: Toggle para activar/desactivar webhook + input numérico para intervalo de poll.
 7: 
 8: ## Archivos a modificar
 9: 
10: ### 1. Migración: `database/migrations/2026_07_XX_add_webhook_settings_to_whatsapp_credentials.php`
11: Nuevo archivo. Añade 2 columnas a `whatsapp_credentials`:
12: ```php
13: $table->boolean('webhook_enabled')->default(true);
14: $table->unsignedSmallInteger('poll_interval')->default(10); // segundos
15: ```
16: 
17: ### 2. Modelo: `app/Models/WhatsAppCredential.php`
18: - Añadir `webhook_enabled` y `poll_interval` a `$fillable`
19: - Añadir cast `webhook_enabled => 'boolean'`, `poll_interval => 'integer'`
20: - Método estático `webhookEnabled(): bool` que retorna `self::get()->webhook_enabled`
21: - Método estático `pollInterval(): int` que retorna `self::get()->poll_interval` (con clamp 5-60)
22: 
23: ### 3. Componente settings: `app/Livewire/Settings/TwilioCredentialSettings.php`
24: - Nueva propiedad pública `bool $webhook_enabled = true`
25: - Nueva propiedad pública `int $poll_interval = 10`
26: - En `mount()`: leer valores de `WhatsAppCredential`
27: - En `save()`: validar y guardar ambos campos
28: - Validación: `poll_interval` entre 5 y 60 segundos
29: 
30: ### 4. Vista settings: `resources/views/settings/twilio-credential-settings.blade.php`
31: En la sección "Callback URL", añadir debajo del input existente:
32: - Toggle `wire:model="webhook_enabled"` → "Webhook activado"
33: - Input numérico `wire:model="poll_interval"` → "Intervalo de sincronización (segundos)" — solo visible si webhook desactivado
34: - Texto explicativo: "Sin webhook, se consulta la API de Twilio cada X segundos"
35: 
36: ### 5. Vista citas: `resources/views/livewire/client-appointments.blade.php`
37: Cambiar línea 2:
38: ```
39: wire:poll.10s="autoSync"
40: ```
41: Por:
42: ```
43: wire:poll.{{ $pollInterval }}s="autoSync"
44: ```
45: La variable `$pollInterval` se pasa desde el componente Livewire.
46: 
47: ### 6. Componente citas: `app/Livewire/ClientAppointments.php`
48: - En `mount()` o `render()`: leer `WhatsAppCredential::pollInterval()` y pasarlo a la vista
49: - Si `webhook_enabled` es true → el poll sigue funcionando como fallback (o se puede deshabilitar)
50: - El `autoSync()` sigue llamando `syncAll()` que hace polling a la API — esto es el fallback cuando no hay webhook
51: 
52: ### 7. Artisan command: `app/Console/Commands/SyncWhatsAppDeliveryStatus.php`
53: - Añadir check: si `webhook_enabled` está activo, el command aún corre como fallback (no cambiar)
54: 
55: ## Lógica de negocio
56: 
57: | webhook_enabled | poll_interval | Comportamiento |
58: |---|---|---|
59: | true | X | Webhook recibe datos instantáneamente. `wire:poll` sigue como fallback cada Xs |
60: | false | X | No hay webhook. `wire:poll` consulta API Twilio cada Xs |
61: 
62: **Nota**: El toggle NO desactiva el poll completamente — siempre hay un fallback por si el webhook falla. Lo que cambia es:
63: - **Webhook ON**: los datos llegan vía webhook, el poll es solo respaldo
64: - **Webhook OFF**: los datos SOLO llegan vía poll a la API de Twilio

70: 4. Con webhook ON → guardar, enviar mensaje WhatsApp, respuesta se procesa via webhook
71: 5. Con webhook OFF → cambiar intervalo a 5s, guardar, enviar mensaje, respuesta llega via poll cada 5s
72: 6. Verificar que el toast muestra el guardado correcto
73: 7. Ejecutar `vendor/bin/pint --dirty --format agent` después de cada cambio PHP

23:         $deletedWhatsAppMessages = DB::table('whatsapp_messages')->delete();
24:         $deletedAppointments = DB::table('appointments')->delete();
25:         $deletedClients = DB::table('clients')->delete();
26:         $deletedUsers = DB::table('users')->delete();
27: 
28:         $seeded = $this->callSilent('db:seed', [
29:             '--class' => DatabaseSeeder::class,
30:             '--force' => true,
31:         ]);
32: 
33:         if ($seeded !== self::SUCCESS) {
34:             $this->error('DatabaseSeeder failed.');
35: 
36:             return self::FAILURE;
37:         }
38: 
39:         $this->info(sprintf(
40:             'Deleted %d user(s), %d client(s), %d WhatsApp message(s) and %d appointment(s).',
41:             $deletedUsers,
42:             $deletedClients,
43:             $deletedWhatsAppMessages,
44:             $deletedAppointments,
45:         ));
46:         $this->info('DatabaseSeeder executed.');
47: 
48:         return self::SUCCESS;
49:     }
50: }
````

23:         ]);

31:         $request->session()->regenerate();

37:         ]);
38:

## File: app/Livewire/Settings/TableBackup.php
````php
  1: <?php
  2: 
  3: namespace App\Livewire\Settings;
  4: 
  5: use App\Models\Appointment;
  6: use App\Models\Client;
  7: use App\Models\User;
  8: use Livewire\Component;
  9: use Livewire\WithFileUploads;
 10: 
 11: class TableBackup extends Component
 12: {
 13:     use WithFileUploads;
 14: 
 15:     private const BOOL_FIELDS = [
 16:         'is_admin', 'enviado', 'entregado', 'activo', 'cita_activa',
 17:         'confirmada', 'pendiente_reprogramacion',
 18:     ];
 19: 
 20:     public string $selectedTable = 'clients';
 21: 
 22:     public $importFile;
 23: 
 24:     public string $importStatus = '';
 25: 
 26:     public int $importStatusNonce = 0;
 27: 
 28:     public bool $confirmImport = false;
 29: 
 30:     public array $tables = [
 31:         'clients' => 'Clientes',
 32:         'appointments' => 'Citas',
 33:         'users' => 'Usuarios',
 34:     ];
 35: 
 36:     public function mount(): void
 37:     {
 38:         //
 39:     }
 40: 
 41:     public function updatedImportFile(): void
 42:     {
 43:         $this->confirmImport = false;
 44:         $this->importStatus = '';
 45:     }
 46: 
 47:     public function importTable(): void
 48:     {
 49:         abort_unless(auth()->user()?->is_admin, 403);
 50: 
 51:         if (! $this->importFile) {
 52:             $this->importStatus = 'Selecciona un archivo.';
 53:             $this->importStatusNonce++;
 54: 
 55:             return;
 56:         }
 57: 
 58:         if (! $this->confirmImport) {
 59:             $this->confirmImport = true;
 60:             $this->importStatus = 'Pulsa de nuevo en Importar para confirmar.';
 61:             $this->importStatusNonce++;
 62: 
 63:             return;
 64:         }
 65: 
 66:         $originalName = $this->importFile->getClientOriginalName();
 67:         $extension = strtolower(pathinfo($originalName, PATHINFO_EXTENSION));
 68: 
 69:         if ($extension === 'json') {
 70:             $this->importFromJson();
 71:         } elseif ($extension === 'csv') {
 72:             $this->importFromCsv();
 73:         } else {
 74:             $this->importStatus = 'Formato no soportado. Usa .json o .csv.';
 75:             $this->importStatusNonce++;
 76:             $this->confirmImport = false;
 77:         }
 78:     }
 79: 
 80:     private function importFromJson(): void
 81:     {
 82:         $json = file_get_contents($this->importFile->getRealPath());
 83: 
 84:         if ($json === false) {
 85:             $this->importStatus = 'No se pudo leer el archivo.';
 86:             $this->importStatusNonce++;
 87:             $this->confirmImport = false;
 88: 
 89:             return;
 90:         }
 91: 
 92:         $records = json_decode($json, true);
 93: 
 94:         if (json_last_error() !== JSON_ERROR_NONE) {
 95:             $this->importStatus = 'JSON inválido: '.json_last_error_msg();
 96:             $this->importStatusNonce++;
 97:             $this->confirmImport = false;
 98: 
 99:             return;
100:         }
101: 
102:         $this->applyRecords($records);
103:     }
104: 
105:     private function importFromCsv(): void
106:     {
107:         $handle = fopen($this->importFile->getRealPath(), 'r');
108: 
109:         if ($handle === false) {
110:             $this->importStatus = 'No se pudo leer el CSV.';
111:             $this->importStatusNonce++;
112:             $this->confirmImport = false;
113: 
114:             return;
115:         }
116: 
117:         $headings = fgetcsv($handle);
118: 
119:         if ($headings === false) {
120:             fclose($handle);
121:             $this->importStatus = 'CSV vacío.';
122:             $this->importStatusNonce++;
123:             $this->confirmImport = false;
124: 
125:             return;
126:         }
127: 
128:         $records = [];
129: 
130:         while (($row = fgetcsv($handle)) !== false) {
131:             $record = array_combine($headings, $row);
132:             $records[] = $this->unflattenFromCsv($record);
133:         }
134: 
135:         fclose($handle);
136:         $this->applyRecords($records);
137:     }
138: 
139:     private function applyRecords(array $records): void
140:     {
141:         $count = count($records);
142: 
143:         match ($this->selectedTable) {
144:             'clients' => $this->importClients($records),
145:             'appointments' => $this->importAppointments($records),
146:             'users' => $this->importUsers($records),
147:         };
148: 
149:         $this->importStatus = "{$count} registro(s) importado(s) en {$this->tables[$this->selectedTable]}.";
150:         $this->importStatusNonce++;
151:         $this->confirmImport = false;
152:         $this->importFile = null;
153:     }
154: 
155:     private function importClients(array $records): void
156:     {
157:         foreach ($records as $record) {
158:             Client::upsertFromImport($record);
159:         }
160:     }
161: 
162:     private function importAppointments(array $records): void
163:     {
164:         foreach ($records as $record) {
165:             $existing = null;
166: 
167:             if (! empty($record['id'])) {
168:                 $existing = Appointment::find($record['id']);
169:             }
170: 
171:             $data = [
172:                 'client_id' => $record['client_id'],
173:                 'fecha' => $record['fecha'],
174:                 'hora' => $record['hora'],
175:                 'fecha_original' => $record['fecha_original'] ?? null,
176:                 'hora_original' => $record['hora_original'] ?? null,
177:                 'enviado' => $record['enviado'] ?? false,
178:                 'entregado' => $record['entregado'] ?? false,
179:                 'activo' => $record['activo'] ?? true,
180:                 'cita_activa' => $record['cita_activa'] ?? true,
181:                 'confirmada' => $record['confirmada'] ?? false,
182:                 'pendiente_reprogramacion' => $record['pendiente_reprogramacion'] ?? false,
183:             ];
184: 
185:             if ($existing) {
186:                 $existing->update($data);
187:             } else {
188:                 unset($record['id']);
189:                 Appointment::create($data);
190:             }
191:         }
192:     }
193: 
194:     private function importUsers(array $records): void
195:     {
196:         foreach ($records as $record) {
197:             $existing = null;
198: 
199:             if (! empty($record['id'])) {
200:                 $existing = User::find($record['id']);
201:             }
202: 
203:             $data = [
204:                 'name' => $record['name'] ?? '',
205:                 'email' => $record['email'] ?? '',
206:                 'is_admin' => $record['is_admin'] ?? false,
207:             ];
208: 
209:             if ($existing) {
210:                 $existing->update($data);
211:             } else {
212:                 User::create($data);
213:             }
214:         }
215:     }
216: 
217:     private function unflattenFromCsv(array $row): array
218:     {
219:         $result = [];
220: 
221:         foreach ($row as $key => $value) {
222:             if ($value === '' || $value === null) {
223:                 $result[$key] = null;
224:             } elseif (in_array($key, self::BOOL_FIELDS, true)) {
225:                 $result[$key] = $value === '1';
226:             } else {
227:                 $result[$key] = $value;
228:             }
229:         }
230: 
231:         return $result;
232:     }
233: 
234:     public function render()
235:     {
236:         return view('settings.table-backup');
237:     }
238: }
````

## File: app/Services/ClientDataDeletionService.php
````php
 1: <?php
 2: 
 3: namespace App\Services;
 4: 
 5: use App\Models\Appointment;
 6: use App\Models\Client;
 7: use App\Models\WhatsAppMessage;
 8: use Illuminate\Support\Collection;
 9: use Illuminate\Support\Facades\DB;
10: 
11: class ClientDataDeletionService
12: {
13:     /**
14:      * @param  iterable<int, int|string>  $appointmentIds
15:      */
16:     public function deleteAppointments(iterable $appointmentIds, ?int $clientId = null): int
17:     {
18:         $appointmentIds = $this->appointmentIds($appointmentIds, $clientId);
19: 
20:         if ($appointmentIds->isEmpty()) {
21:             return 0;
22:         }
23: 
24:         return DB::transaction(function () use ($appointmentIds): int {
25:             $this->deleteWhatsAppMessagesForAppointments($appointmentIds);
26: 
27:             return Appointment::query()
28:                 ->whereKey($appointmentIds)
29:                 ->delete();
30:         });
31:     }
32: 
33:     public function deleteClientById(int $clientId): bool
34:     {
35:         return DB::transaction(function () use ($clientId): bool {
36:             $client = Client::query()->find($clientId);
37: 
38:             if (! $client) {
39:                 return false;
40:             }
41: 
42:             $appointmentIds = $client->appointments()->pluck('id');
43: 
44:             $messageIds = WhatsAppMessage::query()
45:                 ->where('client_id', $client->id)
46:                 ->when($appointmentIds->isNotEmpty(), fn ($query) => $query->orWhereIn('appointment_id', $appointmentIds))
47:                 ->pluck('id');
48: 
49:             WhatsAppMessage::query()
50:                 ->whereIn('id', $messageIds)
51:                 ->orWhereIn('parent_id', $messageIds)
52:                 ->delete();
53: 
54:             return (bool) $client->delete();
55:         });
56:     }
57: 
58:     /**
59:      * @param  iterable<int, int|string>  $appointmentIds
60:      * @return Collection<int, int>
61:      */
62:     private function appointmentIds(iterable $appointmentIds, ?int $clientId): Collection
63:     {
64:         $ids = collect($appointmentIds)
65:             ->map(fn (int|string $id): int => (int) $id)
66:             ->filter()
67:             ->unique()
68:             ->values();
69: 
70:         if ($ids->isEmpty()) {
71:             return collect();
72:         }
73: 
74:         return Appointment::query()
75:             ->when($clientId, fn ($query) => $query->where('client_id', $clientId))
76:             ->whereKey($ids)
77:             ->pluck('id');
78:     }
79: 
80:     /**
81:      * @param  Collection<int, int>  $appointmentIds
82:      */
83:     private function deleteWhatsAppMessagesForAppointments(Collection $appointmentIds): void
84:     {
85:         $messageIds = WhatsAppMessage::query()
86:             ->whereIn('appointment_id', $appointmentIds)
87:             ->pluck('id');
88: 
89:         WhatsAppMessage::query()
90:             ->whereIn('appointment_id', $appointmentIds)
91:             ->when($messageIds->isNotEmpty(), fn ($query) => $query->orWhereIn('parent_id', $messageIds))
92:             ->delete();
93:     }
94: }
````

## File: app/Traits/ValidatesSelectableDate.php
````php
 1: <?php
 2: 
 3: namespace App\Traits;
 4: 
 5: use Carbon\Carbon;
 6: use Illuminate\Support\Facades\Validator;
 7: use Illuminate\Validation\ValidationException;
 8: 
 9: trait ValidatesSelectableDate
10: {
11:     private function validateSelectableDate(string $date, string $field): void
12:     {
13:         $validator = Validator::make([$field => $date], [
14:             $field => [
15:                 function (string $attribute, mixed $value, \Closure $fail): void {
16:                     if (Carbon::parse((string) $value)->isSunday()) {
17:                         $fail('No se pueden seleccionar citas en domingo.');
18:                     }
19:                 },
20:             ],
21:         ]);
22: 
23:         if ($validator->fails()) {
24:             throw new ValidationException($validator);
25:         }
26:     }
27: }
````

  1: <div wire:poll.{{ $pollInterval }}s="pollUpdates">

  4:             x-data="{
  5:             x: 16,
  6:             y: 16,
  7:             dragging: false,
  8:             offsetX: 0,
  9:             offsetY: 0,
 10:             init() {
 11:                 const savedX = parseInt(localStorage.getItem('unread-responses-notice:x') || '', 10);
 12:                 const savedY = parseInt(localStorage.getItem('unread-responses-notice:y') || '', 10);
 13:                 this.x = Number.isFinite(savedX) ? savedX : 16;
 14:                 this.y = Number.isFinite(savedY) ? savedY : 16;
 15:                 this.clampToViewport();
 16:                 window.addEventListener('resize', () => this.clampToViewport());
 17:             },
 18:             startDrag(event) {
 19:                 this.dragging = true;
 20:                 this.offsetX = event.clientX - this.x;
 21:                 this.offsetY = event.clientY - this.y;
 22:             },
 23:             drag(event) {
 24:                 if (!this.dragging) return;
 25:                 this.x = event.clientX - this.offsetX;
 26:                 this.y = event.clientY - this.offsetY;
 27:                 this.clampToViewport();
 28:             },
 29:             stopDrag() {
 30:                 if (!this.dragging) return;
 31:                 this.dragging = false;
 32:                 localStorage.setItem('unread-responses-notice:x', String(this.x));
 33:                 localStorage.setItem('unread-responses-notice:y', String(this.y));
 34:             },
 35:             clampToViewport() {
 36:                 const panel = this.$refs.panel;
 37:                 if (!panel) return;
 38:                 const maxX = Math.max(8, window.innerWidth - panel.offsetWidth - 8);
 39:                 const maxY = Math.max(8, window.innerHeight - panel.offsetHeight - 8);
 40:                 this.x = Math.min(Math.max(8, this.x), maxX);
 41:                 this.y = Math.min(Math.max(8, this.y), maxY);
 42:             },
 43:         }"
 44:             x-on:pointermove.window="drag($event)"
 45:             x-on:pointerup.window="stopDrag()"
 46:             x-on:pointercancel.window="stopDrag()"
 47:             x-on:mouseleave.window="stopDrag()"
 48:             x-bind:style="`left:${x}px; top:${y}px;`"

## File: tests/Feature/AdminDatabaseBackupTest.php
````php
 1: <?php
 2: 
 3: namespace Tests\Feature;
 4: 
 5: use App\Models\Appointment;
 6: use App\Models\Client;
 7: use App\Models\User;
 8: use Illuminate\Foundation\Testing\RefreshDatabase;
 9: use Tests\TestCase;
10: use ZipArchive;
11: 
12: class AdminDatabaseBackupTest extends TestCase
13: {
14:     use RefreshDatabase;
15: 
16:     public function test_admin_can_download_a_sqlite_backup_zip(): void
17:     {
18:         $admin = User::factory()->create(['is_admin' => true]);
19:         $client = Client::query()->create([
20:             'nombre' => 'Ana',
21:             'apellidos' => 'López',
22:             'telefono' => '+34 600 000 000',
23:             'fecha' => today()->toDateString(),
24:             'hora' => '10:30:00',
25:         ]);
26: 
27:         Appointment::query()->create([
28:             'client_id' => $client->id,
29:             'fecha' => today()->addDay()->toDateString(),
30:             'hora' => '11:00:00',
31:             'enviado' => false,
32:             'activo' => true,
33:         ]);
34: 
35:         $response = $this->actingAs($admin)
36:             ->get(route('admin.export.database'))
37:             ->assertDownload('citas-dentista-backup.zip');
38: 
39:         $zipPath = $response->baseResponse->getFile()->getPathname();
40:         $zip = new ZipArchive;
41: 
42:         $this->assertTrue($zip->open($zipPath));
43: 
44:         $sql = $zip->getFromName('citas-dentista-backup.sql');
45: 
46:         $this->assertIsString($sql);
47:         $this->assertStringContainsString('PRAGMA foreign_keys=OFF;', $sql);
48:         $this->assertStringContainsString('INSERT INTO "users"', $sql);
49:         $this->assertStringContainsString('INSERT INTO "clients"', $sql);
50:         $this->assertStringContainsString('INSERT INTO "appointments"', $sql);
51:         $this->assertStringContainsString($admin->email, $sql);
52:         $this->assertStringContainsString('Ana', $sql);
53: 
54:         $zip->close();
55:     }
56: }
````

 78:             'telefono' => '+34600111222',
 79:         ]);
 80:         $appointment = $this->createAppointment($client);
 81: 
 82:         $parent = $this->createWhatsAppMessage($client, $appointment);
 83:         $child = $this->createWhatsAppMessage($client, parent: $parent);
 84: 
 85:         app(ClientDataDeletionService::class)->deleteAppointments([$appointment->id], $client->id);
 86: 
 87:         $this->assertModelMissing($parent);
 88:         $this->assertModelMissing($child);
 89:     }
 90: 
 91:     private function createAppointment(Client $client, string $fecha = '2026-07-01'): Appointment
 92:     {
 93:         return Appointment::query()->create([
 94:             'client_id' => $client->id,
 95:             'fecha' => $fecha,
 96:             'hora' => '10:15',
 97:             'enviado' => false,
 98:             'activo' => true,
 99:         ]);
100:     }
101: 
102:     private function createWhatsAppMessage(Client $client, ?Appointment $appointment = null, ?WhatsAppMessage $parent = null): WhatsAppMessage
103:     {
104:         return WhatsAppMessage::query()->create([
105:             'client_id' => $client->id,
106:             'appointment_id' => $appointment?->id,
107:             'parent_id' => $parent?->id,
108:             'nombre' => $client->nombre,
109:             'apellidos' => $client->apellidos,
110:             'telefono' => $client->telefono,
111:             'scheduled_for' => now()->addDay(),
112:             'message' => 'Recordatorio',
113:             'source' => WhatsAppMessage::SOURCE_APPOINTMENT,
114:             'status' => WhatsAppMessage::STATUS_SENT,
115:         ]);
116:     }
117: }
````

55:     }
56:
